title: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables

sections.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
questions.prompt: 60 students were asked whether they have a curfew and whether they have chores. 36 have a curfew. 24 of the students with a curfew have chores. 8 of the students without a curfew have chores. Complete the two-way table.
questions.prompt_markup:
60 students were asked whether they have a curfew and whether they have chores. 36 have a curfew. 24 of the students with a curfew have chores. 8 of the students without a curfew have chores.
Complete the two-way table.
questions.correct_answer: Curfew: 24 chores, 12 no chores, 36 total. No curfew: 8 chores, 16 no chores, 24 total. Totals: 32 chores, 28 no chores, 60 in all.

figure.description: Table.  | Chores | No chores | Total / Curfew |            |            |            / No curfew |            |            |            / Total |            |            |           .

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
questions.prompt: 50 students were asked whether they prefer summer or winter. 22 are in Grade 7 and 28 are in Grade 8. 15 of the Grade 7 students and 18 of the Grade 8 students prefer summer. Complete the two-way table.
questions.prompt_markup:
50 students were asked whether they prefer summer or winter. 22 are in Grade 7 and 28 are in Grade 8. 15 of the Grade 7 students and 18 of the Grade 8 students prefer summer.
Complete the two-way table.
questions.correct_answer: Grade 7: 15 summer, 7 winter, 22 total. Grade 8: 18 summer, 10 winter, 28 total. Totals: 33 summer, 17 winter, 50 in all.

figure.description: Table.  | Summer | Winter | Total / Grade 7 |            |            |            / Grade 8 |            |            |            / Total |            |            |           .

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
questions.prompt: 90 people were asked whether they exercise daily and whether they eat breakfast. 40 exercise daily. 30 of the people who exercise daily eat breakfast. 50 of the 90 people eat breakfast. Complete the two-way table.
questions.prompt_markup:
90 people were asked whether they exercise daily and whether they eat breakfast. 40 exercise daily. 30 of the people who exercise daily eat breakfast. 50 of the 90 people eat breakfast.
Complete the two-way table.
questions.correct_answer: Exercises: 30 breakfast, 10 no breakfast, 40 total. Does not: 20 breakfast, 30 no breakfast, 50 total. Totals: 50 breakfast, 40 no breakfast, 90 in all.

figure.description: Table.  | Breakfast | No breakfast | Total / Exercises |            |            |            / Does not |            |            |            / Total |            |            |           .

questions.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
questions.prompt: Ten students answered two questions: "Do you have a pet?" and "Do you have a sibling?" Their answers (pet, sibling) are: yes–yes, yes–no, no–no, yes–yes, no–yes, yes–yes, no–no, no–yes, yes–no, no–no Complete the two-way table.
questions.prompt_markup:
Ten students answered two questions: "Do you have a pet?" and "Do you have a sibling?" Their answers (pet, sibling) are:
yes–yes, yes–no, no–no, yes–yes, no–yes, yes–yes, no–no, no–yes, yes–no, no–no
Complete the two-way table.
questions.correct_answer: Pet: 3 sibling, 2 no sibling, 5 total. No pet: 2 sibling, 3 no sibling, 5 total. Totals: 5 sibling, 5 no sibling, 10 in all.

figure.description: Table.  | Sibling | No sibling | Total / Pet |            |            |            / No pet |            |            |            / Total |            |            |           .
